name: Ahmad Shawqi
bio: Ahmad Shawqi was born in Cairo in 1285 AH (1868 CE) and grew up in the shadow of Egypt's ruling house; he wrote that he had heard his father trace the family back “to the Kurds, then the Arabs”. He studied law in Egypt and then in Montpellier, where Khedive Tawfiq sent him, and came back to head the European bureau at the court of Khedive Abbas Hilmi; when Abbas was deposed during the First World War, Shawqi was told to live somewhere other than Egypt, spent 1915 to late 1919 in Spain, and on his return sat in the Senate. Called the Prince of Poets, he wrote praise, love poems, elegies and descriptions, and then poems on the events of Egypt, the East and the Muslim world that everyone repeated; they were collected as al-Shawqiyyat. He was the first to excel at verse drama in Arabic; among his plays are The Death of Cleopatra and Majnun Layla. He died in Cairo in 1351 AH (1932 CE).
